bug_classes.definition: A sensitive operation trusts a peer whose identity has not been authenticated.
A one-use authorization is replayed or rebound to a different operation.
Secret credential material crosses an unauthorized observation or data boundary.
An untrusted origin or local socket principal obtains reservation authority.
Unvalidated event data is treated as control authority.
Negotiated or received media is routed through an unvalidated address or codec boundary.
Concurrent or stale reservation transitions grant conflicting ownership.
Recovery reuses a resource while a previous operation may still own it.
An unsettled operation holds admission indefinitely without bounded recovery.

claims.statement: Every credential-bearing ARI HTTP/WSS request authenticates the intended peer through the canonical transport before credentials are released; trust provisioning cannot introduce a downgrade.
preserves: Valid peer subscription, call lifecycle and owned cleanup remain reachable.

claims.statement: A reservation nonce authorizes exactly one call to its bound destination; authoritative readback comes from authenticated ARI, never Stasis arguments.
preserves: A valid bound reservation can complete its intended call.

claims.statement: Provider credentials stay out of logs, browser SIP messages, ARI variables and errors; transient secrets are cleared after use.
preserves: Legitimate provider authentication uses the credential only through SIP/TLS.

claims.statement: Reservations require the configured HTTPS Origin/Host and client header; their Unix socket is owner-only 0600 with verified identity/link count and stale-socket refusal.
ARI uses the fixed IPv4 loopback destination and canonical authenticated transport, and validates all browser/Stasis admission fields before granting control.
preserves: Valid Stasis events and legitimate browser calls are admitted.

claims.statement: Provider transport requires TLS 1.2 or newer, trusted roots, hostname and host-allowlist validation; insecure verification cannot be enabled.
Provider media accepts only the permitted public PCMA answer, rejects private/loopback/multicast/unspecified addresses and multiple codecs, and admits RTP only from the negotiated source.
preserves: Valid public single-PCMA media remains usable.

claims.statement: Reservation consumption and ownership transitions are atomic, prevent double-spend/TOCTOU grants, and retain exclusivity while teardown is unsettled.
preserves: A settled call releases its slot; any bounded recovery preserves exclusive call ownership.

claims.statement: An ambiguous call cannot monopolize admission indefinitely; bounded recovery must exclude a still-live prior provider leg before the slot is reused.
preserves: Calls remain exclusive during the recovery bound and new legitimate reservations can eventually proceed.
